intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera, stopping at the Red Beach and White Beach for swimming and snorkeling. The evening departure lets you enjoy the world-famous Oia sunset from the water while avoiding the intense midday heat. Light snacks and local wine are typically included. Indoor alternative: visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera in Fira if weather turns.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip
experiences.description: Take an early morning boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches enclosed by towering white cliffs. Arrive before the crowds and midday heat for the best experience. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters and explore the famous rusted shipwreck. Indoor alternative: visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos in the afternoon.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete
experiences.description: Join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (Cretan rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and kalitsounia (cheese pastries) using locally sourced ingredients. Enjoy your creations for lunch with local raki. Held indoors or under shaded pergolas, ideal for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the stunning pink-sand Elafonissi Beach at sunrise or early morning when the lagoon is calm, uncrowded, and the light is magical. Snorkel through the shallow turquoise lagoon teeming with sea life and explore the small islet connected by a sandbar. Rent snorkel gear locally for a minimal cost. Indoor alternative for midday: explore the nearby Chrysoskalitissa Monastery, a cool stone structure with cultural significance.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from below. Grab a cheap souvlaki wrap from a street kiosk to ease into Greek food culture.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or grab a coffee and koulouri (sesame bread ring) from an airport kiosk for €1–2
meals.lunch: Skip or grab a snack at the airport
meals.dinner: Souvlaki wrap (gyros pita) from a street vendor in Monastiraki — €2.50–3.50

day_by_day.notes: Use the Metro Line 3 from the airport to Monastiraki station for about €9 — cheapest and fastest option into the city center. Buy a 5-day transit pass if you plan to use public transport frequently.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Combined ticket costs €20 but covers multiple archaeological sites valid for 5 days — great value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (covered by the combined ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for free browsing and local atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Psiri neighborhood for dinner. Explore the lively tavernas and ouzeries. Try a classic Greek salad and grilled sardines at a local taverna.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local bakery — €2–3
meals.lunch: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and tiropita (cheese pie) from a street bakery near the Agora — €2–4
meals.dinner: Grilled sardines, Greek salad, and house wine at a Psiri taverna — €10–14 per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable shoes for the Acropolis — the marble paths are slippery. Bring a refillable water bottle; temperatures can reach 23°C+ by midday. The combined archaeological ticket saves significant money if you plan to visit multiple sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (€12 entry, free on certain days). One of the world's greatest collections of Greek antiquities — allow 2–3 hours. Located in Exarchia neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Exarchia and Kolonaki neighborhoods on foot. Browse the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street — a vibrant, authentic market with fresh produce, meat, fish, and spices. Great for people-watching and photography.
day_by_day.evening: Take the funicular up Lycabettus Hill (€7 round trip) for panoramic sunset views over Athens. Alternatively, hike up for free. Return to Monastiraki for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) at a local café — €3–4
meals.lunch: Fresh produce and snacks from the Central Market — €3–5, or a cheap souvlaki nearby
meals.dinner: Moussaka and a carafe of house wine at a traditional taverna in Monastiraki — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays — check the schedule. The Central Market is most lively in the morning but open through the afternoon. Lycabettus sunset is spectacular on clear evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early KTEL bus or train from Athens to Nafplio (approximately 2–2.5 hours, €13–15). Nafplio is a stunning coastal town in the Peloponnese — one of Greece's most charming destinations. Check into a budget guesthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful old town on foot. Visit the Venetian Bourtzi fortress visible from the harbor (boat trip €5 return). Walk along the waterfront promenade and browse the neoclassical streets.
day_by_day.evening: Climb the 999 steps up to Palamidi Fortress (€8 entry) for breathtaking views over the Argolic Gulf at sunset. Return to town for dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and pastry before the bus at Athens bus terminal — €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood mezedes (small plates) at a harbor-side café in Nafplio — €8–12
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus, tzatziki, and pita at a local taverna in Nafplio old town — €12–15

day_by_day.notes: Book the KTEL bus ticket in advance online or at the Athens Kifissos bus terminal. Nafplio is very walkable — no need for taxis. The Palamidi climb is strenuous but rewarding; go in the late afternoon to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Epidaurus (30 km from Nafplio, local bus €3–4 each way). Visit the ancient Theatre of Epidaurus — one of the best-preserved ancient theatres in the world with remarkable acoustics. Entry €12 (covered by combined ticket if purchased in Athens).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, free pebble beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Swim in the clear Aegean waters. Alternatively, rent a pedal boat for €5–8/hour.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a leisurely evening in Nafplio's Syntagma Square. Try local street food and ice cream. Watch locals gather for the evening volta (stroll).

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt, honey, and fresh fruit at the guesthouse or a local café — €3–4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack from a bakery before the Epidaurus trip — €3–5
meals.dinner: Fresh catch of the day at a harbor taverna — €11–15 per person

day_by_day.notes: Check the local bus schedule to Epidaurus in advance — buses are infrequent. Bring sunscreen and a hat for the beach. Arvanitia Beach can get busy in the afternoon; arrive early for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Take the bus back to Athens (Kifissos terminal) and then connect to Piraeus port. Board the ferry to Santorini (approximately 5–8 hours depending on ferry type). Book economy/deck class tickets in advance — €35–50 one way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Santorini (Thira port). Take the local bus (€1.80) from the port up to Fira, the island's capital. Check into a budget hostel or studio apartment in Fira or nearby Karterados village (cheaper than Oia).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Fira on foot. Walk along the caldera rim for stunning volcanic views. Watch the famous Santorini sunset from the caldera edge — free and spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry at Piraeus port before boarding — €3–4
meals.lunch: Packed snacks or ferry café food on board — €5–8
meals.dinner: Gyros or souvlaki from a local fast-food spot in Fira — €3–5 (avoid caldera-view restaurants which are very expensive)

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets well in advance for June — Santorini is extremely popular. Slow ferries are much cheaper than high-speed catamarans. Stay in Karterados or Messaria villages for significantly cheaper accommodation than Fira or Oia.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus (€1.80) to Perissa Beach on the south coast — one of Santorini's best free black sand beaches. Arrive early to claim a good spot. The beach is long and less crowded at the northern end.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue relaxing at Perissa Beach. Swim in the warm Aegean waters. Walk to the adjacent Perivolos Beach for a change of scenery. Both beaches have free access with optional paid sunbed rental (€5–8/pair).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira by bus. Walk the scenic caldera path from Fira toward Imerovigli (about 3 km, free). Watch the sunset from Skaros Rock viewpoint — a hidden gem away from the Oia crowds.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, cheese, and tomatoes from a local mini-market — €3–4
meals.lunch: Fresh fish or calamari at a beachside taverna at Perissa — €10–14
meals.dinner: Fava (yellow split pea dip), stuffed tomatoes, and local wine at a Fira taverna away from the main tourist strip — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Santorini's local bus network (KTEL) is excellent and very cheap — buy tickets on board. Perissa black sand gets extremely hot by midday — bring sandals. Avoid the overpriced restaurants directly on the caldera rim.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Fira to Oia trail (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours). This free coastal path offers the most spectacular views of the caldera, volcanic cliffs, and whitewashed villages. Start early to avoid the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Oia and explore the iconic blue-domed churches and narrow alleyways. Browse the local art galleries and craft shops (window shopping is free). Visit the Oia Castle ruins.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the world-famous Oia sunset from the castle ruins (arrive 1–2 hours early to secure a spot — it gets very crowded). Take the local bus back to Fira (€1.80) after sunset.

meals.breakfast: Energy-boosting breakfast before the hike — Greek yogurt, granola, and coffee at a Fira café — €4–5
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or gyros wrap in Oia (look for spots away from the main tourist drag) — €4–6
meals.dinner: Santorinian tomato fritters (tomatokeftedes) and local Assyrtiko wine at a Fira taverna — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: The Fira-to-Oia hike is moderately challenging — wear proper shoes and bring plenty of water. The path is well-marked but has some uneven sections. Start no later than 8:00 AM to finish before peak heat. The Oia sunset is genuinely magical but extremely crowded — arrive very early.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (approximately 2–3 hours by high-speed ferry, €35–55, or slower ferry for less). Alternatively, take a ferry to Paros for a more budget-friendly island experience. Arrive and check into budget accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Mykonos Town (Chora) on foot — the iconic whitewashed windmills, Little Venice waterfront, and labyrinthine alleyways. Everything is walkable and free to explore.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the famous windmills area. Explore the waterfront bars and tavernas. Mykonos is known for nightlife but budget travelers can enjoy the atmosphere without spending much.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry before the ferry in Santorini — €3–4
meals.lunch: Snack on the ferry or grab a cheap gyros upon arrival in Mykonos — €3–5
meals.dinner: Fresh grilled fish and Greek salad at a local taverna away from the main tourist waterfront — €12–16

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos is one of Greece's most expensive islands — budget carefully. Accommodation is pricier than other islands; book well in advance. Consider Paros as a cheaper alternative with equally beautiful beaches and a charming main town. Ferry connections between islands are frequent in June.

day_by_day.morning: Take the local bus (€1.80) to Paradise Beach or Agios Sostis Beach (free, less commercial, and more beautiful). Agios Sostis has no facilities but is stunning and uncrowded — bring your own food and water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue at the beach or explore the island by local bus. Visit Ano Mera village in the interior — a traditional, non-touristy village with a beautiful monastery (Panagia Tourliani) and cheap local tavernas.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Walk along the Little Venice waterfront at sunset. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of the town without necessarily spending on expensive bars.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, local cheese, and tomatoes from a mini-market — €3–4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Agios Sostis Beach or a cheap taverna in Ano Mera village — €6–10
meals.dinner: Loukoumades (honey doughnuts) as a street snack, plus a simple meal at a budget taverna in Chora — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Agios Sostis Beach has no sunbeds or facilities — bring everything you need. Ano Mera is a great escape from the tourist crowds and significantly cheaper for food. Mykonos local buses are reliable and cheap — the best way to get around on a budget.

day_by_day.morning: Take the ferry back to Athens (Piraeus) — approximately 2.5–5 hours depending on ferry type. Economy class tickets €25–45. Arrive in Athens and check back into a budget hostel in the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Benaki Museum (€9 entry, free on Thursdays) or the Museum of Greek Folk Art (€4) in the Plaka neighborhood. Both offer excellent insight into Greek culture and history.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Thissio neighborhood — a trendy, relaxed area with outdoor cafés and great views of the Acropolis. Walk along the Apostolou Pavlou pedestrian promenade.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and koulouri on the ferry or at Piraeus port — €2–3
meals.lunch: Cheap souvlaki or gyros near Piraeus port before heading into the city — €3–5
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek meze spread (taramosalata, dolmades, grilled vegetables) at a Thissio taverna — €11–14

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry times and book in advance for the return to Athens. The Benaki Museum is free on Thursdays — plan accordingly for extra savings. The Thissio promenade is one of Athens' most pleasant evening walks with stunning Acropolis views.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Cape Sounion (70 km from Athens). Take the KTEL bus from Pedion Areos park (€6.50 each way, approximately 2 hours). Visit the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff above the Aegean Sea (€10 entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim at the small beach below Cape Sounion or at one of the beaches along the Athenian Riviera on the return journey (Vouliagmeni, Varkiza — free public beach access). Take the bus back to Athens.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — revisit your favorite neighborhood. Shop for budget souvenirs at the Monastiraki flea market (open late). Enjoy a farewell dinner in the Psiri or Monastiraki area.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt and honey at the hostel or a nearby café — €3–4
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks at Cape Sounion (the on-site café is overpriced) — €4–6
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner — lamb chops (paidakia), tzatziki, and local wine at a Monastiraki taverna — €14–18

day_by_day.notes: The KTEL bus to Sounion departs from Pedion Areos park (near Viktoria Metro station) — check the schedule in advance. Bring sunscreen and water for Cape Sounion as there is little shade. The sunset at the Temple of Poseidon is legendary — time your visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens. Pack and check out of accommodation. If time allows, visit the Kerameikos Archaeological Site (€8, covered by combined ticket) — Athens' ancient cemetery, often overlooked by tourists but fascinating and peaceful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Athens International Airport via Metro Line 3 from Monastiraki or Syntagma (€9, approximately 40 minutes). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Browse duty-free for last-minute Greek olive oil or honey gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Athens. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, ancient history, and delicious Greek food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — fresh bread, feta cheese, olives, and coffee at a local café near the hostel — €4–6
meals.lunch: Light meal or snack at the airport or grab a final souvlaki near the Metro station before departing — €4–7
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the destination

day_by_day.notes: Keep Metro tickets for the airport journey — Line 3 is the most reliable and cheapest option. Pack any liquid food souvenirs (olive oil, honey) in checked luggage. Greece's tap water is generally safe to drink in Athens and most islands — a great money-saver throughout the trip. Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights): €600–850 per person, including accommodation, transport, food, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens. Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Syntagma area. Freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Admire the illuminated Acropolis from street level. Browse the charming pedestrian lanes of Plaka to get a feel for the city.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: Pick up a quick gyros wrap from a street kiosk near the airport or in Monastiraki (€3–5) — Kostas Souvlaki on Plateia Agias Irinis is a local favorite
meals.dinner: Dinner at Taverna tou Psarra in Plaka — a classic mid-range taverna with grilled meats, Greek salad, and local wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep luggage manageable for public transport. Metro Line 3 from the airport to Monastiraki takes about 40 minutes and costs €9.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — join the guided Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) food tour starting around 9:00 AM. Explore stalls of fresh fish, spices, olives, and cheeses with a local guide. Sample local delicacies including loukoumades, taramosalata, and cured meats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon (book tickets online in advance, €20). Explore the Acropolis Museum afterward (€10) to see stunning artifacts and friezes in an air-conditioned setting — ideal during the warm afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Thisseio neighborhood for sunset views of the Acropolis from the rooftop bars along Apostolou Pavlou pedestrian street. Enjoy the golden hour atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a local kafeneio (Greek coffee + koulouri sesame bread ring, €3–4) near Monastiraki before the food tour
meals.lunch: Lunch is largely covered by tastings during the food tour; supplement with a mezze plate at a market-side ouzeri (€10–14)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant near the Acropolis — mid-range taverna with Acropolis views, excellent moussaka and lamb chops (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets online well in advance to avoid long queues. The food tour typically runs 3–4 hours. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring a hat — June sun can be strong.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (€10) — the heart of ancient Athenian civic life. Explore the remarkably preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Arrive early (opens 8:00 AM) to beat the heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Metro to Piraeus port and board a ferry to the island of Hydra (approximately 1.5–2 hours by Flying Dolphin hydrofoil, €30–35 each way). Arrive in Hydra town — a car-free island with stunning harbor views. Explore the waterfront and climb the hillside alleys.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the magical Hydra harbor at sunset. The island is quieter in the evening after day-trippers leave. Stroll the lit waterfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts at a café near your Athens hotel (€5–7)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled octopus and horiatiki (Greek salad) at a waterfront taverna in Hydra harbor (€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sunset Restaurant in Hydra — seafood pasta, grilled fish, and local white wine with harbor views (€22–28 per person). Stay overnight in Hydra at a mid-range guesthouse (€80–120/night).

day_by_day.notes: Hydra has no motorized vehicles — donkeys and water taxis are the only transport. Book your hydrofoil (Hellenic Seaways or Aegean Flying Dolphins) in advance. Consider staying 2 nights in Hydra.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Hydra's hidden beaches — hike or take a water taxi (€5–8) to Vlychos Beach or Kamini Beach. These small pebble coves offer crystal-clear water and a peaceful morning swim away from crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak or paddleboard (€15–20/hour) along Hydra's coastline. Alternatively, hike up to the Monastery of Profitis Ilias for panoramic island views (about 1.5-hour round trip). Return to the harbor for a late afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Return by hydrofoil to Piraeus and travel onward to Athens airport area or directly to the port of Rafina for your next island connection. Alternatively, spend a second night in Hydra for a more relaxed pace.

meals.breakfast: Fresh pastries and Greek coffee at a bakery in Hydra town (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch — pick up local cheese, olives, bread, and fruit from a small Hydra grocery shop and enjoy on the beach (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Back in Athens — dinner at a neighborhood psistaria (grill house) in Koukaki district, near the Acropolis: grilled lamb chops, tzatziki, and pita (€18–24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Water taxis in Hydra are metered — agree on the price before boarding. The hike to Profitis Ilias is moderately strenuous; bring water and sun protection.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Santorini — take an early ferry from Piraeus (Blue Star Ferries, approximately 5–8 hours, €40–55) or a short domestic flight (30 minutes, €60–100). Arrive in Santorini and check in to a mid-range hotel in Fira or Firostefani with caldera views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fira town — the island's bustling capital. Walk the caldera-edge path from Fira toward Firostefani and Imerovigli (about 3 km, stunning views). Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (€6) to see artifacts from the ancient Akrotiri civilization.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Santorini sunset from the Fira caldera walkway or a rooftop bar. The sunset here is world-class — arrive 30–45 minutes early for a good spot.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita (cheese pie) and coffee from a bakery in Fira before departing Athens (€3–5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the ferry (bring snacks) or a quick souvlaki upon arrival in Fira (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Metaxy Mas restaurant in Exo Gonia village — a beloved local taverna known for authentic Santorinian cuisine: fava, tomatokeftedes, and grilled fish (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Oia is the most famous sunset spot but extremely crowded. Fira and Imerovigli offer equally stunning sunsets with fewer tourists. Book Santorini accommodation well in advance — June is peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri (€12) — a remarkably preserved Bronze Age city buried by the volcanic eruption. Often called the 'Minoan Pompeii.' Arrive at opening (8:00 AM) before the heat builds. Afterward, head to the nearby Red Beach — one of Greece's most dramatic and unique beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Perissa Black Sand Beach on the island's southeastern coast — a long stretch of volcanic black sand with beach bars, sunbeds (€8–12/pair), and calm, warm water. Perfect for swimming and sunbathing.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Fira for the evening. Explore the local shops and art galleries along the caldera path. Enjoy a glass of Assyrtiko white wine — Santorini's signature volcanic grape variety — at a caldera-view wine bar.

meals.breakfast: Full Greek breakfast at your hotel or a café in Fira: eggs, local tomatoes, feta, olives, and bread (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a beach taverna at Perissa: grilled sea bream, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer (€18–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nikolas Restaurant in Fira — a no-frills, authentic local spot with excellent moussaka and stuffed peppers at honest prices (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Red Beach requires a short rocky walk from the parking area — wear sturdy sandals. Perissa is accessible by local bus (KTEL, €1.80) from Fira. Rent an ATV (€25–35/day) for flexible island exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the iconic Fira to Oia trail (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) along the caldera rim. The path passes through Firostefani and Imerovigli with breathtaking views of the caldera, volcanic islands, and Aegean Sea. Start early (7:00–8:00 AM) to avoid midday heat.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Oia and explore the famous blue-domed churches, art galleries, and boutique shops. Visit the Oia Castle ruins. Take a water taxi from Ammoudi Bay (below Oia) for a swim in the clear caldera waters (€5–8 each way down the steps or by donkey).
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from Oia — arrive at the castle ruins by 7:00 PM to secure a spot. The sunset here is legendary. Afterward, enjoy a quieter Oia as day-trippers depart.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — Greek yogurt, honey, and fruit at a Fira café (€6–8)
meals.lunch: Lunch in Oia after the hike at a caldera-view restaurant: fresh pasta with local capers and tomatoes, and a glass of Vinsanto dessert wine (€20–26 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roka Restaurant in Oia — intimate, mid-range spot with creative Greek cuisine and excellent local wine list (€24–32 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Fira–Oia hike is moderately challenging. Bring 2+ liters of water, sunscreen, and a hat. The trail is well-marked but can be rocky in sections. Return to Fira by local bus (€1.80) or taxi (€15–20).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Crete — take a ferry from Santorini to Heraklion (approximately 2 hours by high-speed ferry, €35–50) or a short flight. Check in to a mid-range hotel in Heraklion or the charming old town of Chania (if traveling further west by bus/car).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Palace of Knossos (€15) — the legendary Minoan palace complex, one of Europe's oldest cities. Explore the reconstructed frescoes, throne room, and labyrinthine corridors. Located just 5 km from Heraklion center.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Heraklion's vibrant old town — walk along the Venetian harbor, visit the impressive Koules Fortress (€4), and browse the lively Lion Square (Plateia Venizelou) area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on the ferry or a quick bite at Heraklion port upon arrival
meals.lunch: Traditional Cretan lunch at a taverna near Knossos: dakos (barley rusk with tomato and feta), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and local raki (€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Peskesi Restaurant in Heraklion — a celebrated farm-to-table Cretan restaurant using heirloom ingredients and traditional recipes (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Knossos is best visited with a guide or audio guide (€6) to fully appreciate the complex history. If planning to explore western Crete (Chania), consider renting a car in Heraklion (€35–50/day) for the remaining Crete days.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus west to Chania (approximately 2.5 hours). Explore Chania's stunning Venetian old town — one of the most beautiful in Greece. Walk through the covered market (Agora), the Venetian harbor with its iconic lighthouse, and the narrow lanes of the Jewish Quarter (Evraiki).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Elafonisi Beach (approximately 1.5 hours from Chania by car or organized tour) — a breathtaking lagoon beach with pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise water. Swim and relax in one of Greece's most beautiful natural settings.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for the evening. Stroll the illuminated Venetian harbor at dusk — one of the most romantic settings in all of Greece.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Heraklion before departing, or stop at a roadside bakery en route to Chania for fresh spanakopita (spinach pie, €2–3)
meals.lunch: Picnic at Elafonisi — pack local cheese, olives, and bread from Chania market, or grab food from the small beach kiosk (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tamam Restaurant in Chania old town — housed in a converted Turkish bathhouse, serving creative Cretan-Mediterranean cuisine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Elafonisi is a protected nature reserve — no umbrellas or sunbeds are allowed in the lagoon area. Bring your own shade. The beach can get crowded by midday in June; arrive by 10:00 AM. Stay overnight in Chania (€70–110/night for a mid-range hotel in the old town).

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Samaria Gorge (€5 entry) — one of Europe's longest gorges at 16 km. The hike descends from the Omalos plateau to the coastal village of Agia Roumeli. Start early (buses from Chania depart around 7:30 AM). The hike takes 4–6 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Agia Roumeli on the Libyan Sea coast. Reward yourself with a swim in the crystal-clear waters at the beach here — one of the most satisfying post-hike swims imaginable. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (€15, approximately 1 hour), then bus back to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover in Chania. Enjoy a leisurely evening in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the hike — pack energy bars, nuts, and fruit; grab a coffee and tiropita at the Omalos plateau café before entering the gorge
meals.lunch: Pack a light lunch for the gorge (sandwiches, fruit, plenty of water — 2+ liters essential). There are water springs along the trail.
meals.dinner: Well-deserved dinner at To Maridaki fish taverna in Chania harbor — fresh catch of the day, grilled calamari, and cold Cretan beer (€20–26 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge hike is strenuous — wear proper hiking shoes (not sandals), bring plenty of water, and start early. The gorge is one-way (top to bottom only). Book the Chania bus tour package (€25–30) which includes transport both ways and the ferry.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Botanical Park and Gardens of Crete near Fournes village (€7, 30 minutes from Chania) — a beautiful hillside garden with Cretan flora, fruit trees, and mountain views. A peaceful and scenic morning activity. Alternatively, explore the Chania Archaeological Museum (€4) in the old town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Balos Lagoon — one of Greece's most iconic beaches with a stunning turquoise lagoon and white sand. Take an organized boat trip from Kissamos port (€20–25 round trip, approximately 1.5 hours each way) or drive to the top and hike down (45 minutes). Swim and relax in the lagoon.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Chania — explore the rooftop bars and wine bars along the Venetian harbor. Try a glass of local Cretan wine (Vidiano or Kotsifali varieties).

meals.breakfast: Cretan breakfast at your hotel or a harbor café: local honey, graviera cheese, fresh bread, and mountain herb tea (€7–10)
meals.lunch: Light lunch on the boat or at the small kiosk at Balos (limited options — bring snacks and water). Alternatively, eat before departing at a Kissamos taverna (€14–18)
meals.dinner: Farewell Crete dinner at Ela Restaurant in Chania old town — traditional Cretan mezze spread: dakos, saganaki, lamb with herbs, and local wine (€22–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Balos boat trips typically depart at 10:00 AM and 11:00 AM from Kissamos. Book in advance in June. The lagoon is shallow and warm — perfect for snorkeling. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Travel back to Athens — take an early morning flight from Chania Airport (CHQ) to Athens (45 minutes, €50–80) or a long ferry (9 hours — overnight option). Check back in to your Athens hotel. Visit the National Archaeological Museum (€12) — one of the world's great museums of antiquity, housing the Antikythera Mechanism, Mycenaean gold masks, and stunning ancient sculptures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood — browse boutique shops, visit the Benaki Museum (€9) for Greek art and culture spanning 5,000 years, and take the funicular up Lycabettus Hill (€7 round trip) for the best panoramic views of Athens and the Acropolis.
day_by_day.evening: Final Athens evening — return to the Monastiraki flea market area for last-minute souvenir shopping. Enjoy the lively atmosphere of Psirri neighborhood with its street art, bars, and restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Chania airport or a quick café stop before your flight
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional ouzeri in Monastiraki: grilled octopus, fava dip, and ouzo (€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Special farewell dinner at Varoulko Seaside in Piraeus or Spondi Restaurant in Athens — a step up in quality for the final night, celebrating the trip (€35–50 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Tuesdays — plan accordingly. Lycabettus Hill at sunset offers arguably the best view of Athens. Book the farewell dinner reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a leisurely breakfast and last stroll through the Plaka neighborhood. Visit any remaining sites: the Roman Agora and Tower of the Winds (€8), Hadrian's Arch, or the Temple of Olympian Zeus (€6) — all within walking distance of the city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, head to Athens International Airport via Metro Line 3 from Monastiraki or Syntagma (40 minutes, €9). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before international departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — board your return Air Serbia flight. Reflect on 13 wonderful days of Greek beaches, ancient history, and incredible local food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — fresh loukoumades (honey-drenched doughnuts) from a street vendor in Monastiraki Square (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at the airport — a final gyros wrap or spanakopita to go (€5–8)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Keep some euros for airport transport and last-minute purchases. Greek airports have limited mid-range dining options — eat before arriving if possible. Duty-free shops at Athens airport offer good selections of Greek olive oil, honey, and wine as gifts.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera, stopping at the Red Beach and White Beach for swimming and snorkeling. The evening departure lets you enjoy the world-famous Oia sunset from the water while avoiding the intense midday heat. Light snacks and local wine are typically included. Indoor alternative: visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera in Fira if weather turns.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita from market vendors. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up ingredients for a picnic. Entirely indoors, making it a perfect rain or heat alternative activity.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip
experiences.description: Take an early morning boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed beaches enclosed by towering white cliffs. Arrive before the crowds and midday heat for the best experience. Swim in the crystal-clear turquoise waters and explore the famous rusted shipwreck. Indoor alternative: visit the Byzantine Museum of Zakynthos in the afternoon.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete
experiences.description: Join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes like dakos (Cretan rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and kalitsounia (cheese pastries) using locally sourced ingredients. Enjoy your creations for lunch with local raki. Held indoors or under shaded pergolas, ideal for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach
experiences.description: Visit the stunning pink-sand Elafonissi Beach at sunrise or early morning when the lagoon is calm, uncrowded, and the light is magical. Snorkel through the shallow turquoise lagoon teeming with sea life and explore the small islet connected by a sandbar. Rent snorkel gear locally for a minimal cost. Indoor alternative for midday: explore the nearby Chrysoskalitissa Monastery, a cool stone structure with cultural significance.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your five-star hotel in the Kolonaki or Syntagma district of Athens. Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll around Syntagma Square and the National Garden to acclimate to the city.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first evening with a sunset walk up Lycabettus Hill for panoramic views of Athens. Descend for a sophisticated welcome dinner at a top Athens restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in transit
meals.lunch: Not applicable — in transit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hytra (1 Michelin star, rooftop views of the Acropolis) — savor modern Greek cuisine with tasting menus featuring local ingredients and fine Greek wines

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer. Confirm hotel early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour — join a private or small-group guided tour of the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, spices, and local delicacies with a knowledgeable local guide. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and pick up premium pantry souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon with a private licensed archaeologist guide for an in-depth, crowd-beating experience. Afterward, explore the Acropolis Museum at your own pace, marveling at original friezes and ancient artifacts in a world-class setting.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for boutique shopping and aperitifs at a rooftop bar. Enjoy a refined dinner showcasing modern Greek gastronomy.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — full Greek spread with honey, yogurt, pastries, fresh fruit, and eggs
meals.lunch: Mezze lunch at Tzitzikas kai Mermigas in Monastiraki — creative Greek small plates in a charming setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Varoulko Seaside (1 Michelin star) — celebrated seafood-focused tasting menu by chef Lefteris Lazarou, set along the Piraeus waterfront

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and private guide well in advance. The food tour is best enjoyed on an empty stomach — eat lightly before.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the National Archaeological Museum — one of the world's great museums, housing the Mask of Agamemnon, Antikythera Mechanism, and extraordinary ancient Greek art. Arrange a private curator-led tour for a premium experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Athens International Airport for a short domestic flight to Heraklion, Crete (approximately 45 minutes). Upon arrival, collect your pre-arranged luxury rental car or private transfer and check in to your five-star resort (e.g., Blue Palace Elounda or Domes of Elounda). Spend the afternoon settling in and enjoying the resort's private beach and infinity pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's clifftop bar overlooking the Aegean. Enjoy a leisurely dinner at the resort's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Athens hotel — à la carte with fresh-squeezed juices, Greek yogurt with Cretan honey, and pastries
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport lounge or a quick bite at a Heraklion harbor taverna upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's fine dining restaurant — Cretan-inspired cuisine featuring locally sourced ingredients, fresh seafood, and premium Cretan wines

day_by_day.notes: Book domestic flight Athens–Heraklion in advance. Domes of Elounda or Blue Palace Elounda are exceptional luxury choices in Crete. Confirm resort transfer from Heraklion airport.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in Crete — join a hands-on morning cooking class at a family-run farm or taverna in the Cretan countryside. Learn to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos, lamb with stamnagathi, and loukoumades using fresh local produce, olive oil, and herbs. Enjoy the meal you've prepared as part of the class.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient Minoan Palace of Knossos with a private archaeologist guide — explore Europe's oldest civilization and the legendary labyrinth of King Minos. Afterward, browse the charming streets of Heraklion's old town and visit the Venetian Koules Fortress.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a spa treatment (book in advance) — try a traditional Cretan olive oil massage or thalassotherapy. Dine at a waterfront restaurant in Elounda village.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before the cooking class
meals.lunch: The dishes prepared during the cooking class — a true farm-to-table Cretan feast
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ferryman Taverna in Elounda — legendary waterfront seafood restaurant beloved by locals and discerning travelers alike

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 9:00–13:00. Book in advance through the resort concierge. Knossos is best visited in the afternoon when morning crowds thin.

day_by_day.morning: Early Morning Snorkeling at Elafonissi Beach — depart at sunrise for the stunning pink-sand Elafonissi Beach (approximately 1.5 hours from Elounda by car). Arrive early when the shallow turquoise lagoon is calm and nearly deserted. Snorkel the crystal-clear waters, explore the pink-tinged shoreline, and enjoy the magical morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the scenic western Crete coastline on the drive back, stopping at the charming Venetian harbor town of Rethymno. Wander the old town's narrow alleys, visit the Venetian Fortezza, and browse artisan shops.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a private sunset dinner on your villa terrace or balcony arranged by the resort concierge — a romantic in-room dining experience with Aegean views.

meals.breakfast: Pack a gourmet picnic breakfast from the resort to enjoy at Elafonissi Beach at sunrise
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional taverna in Rethymno old town — try fresh grilled octopus, fried calamari, and local Cretan cheeses
meals.dinner: Private in-villa dining experience arranged by the resort — curated Cretan tasting menu with local wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is approximately 75 km from Elounda — depart by 5:30–6:00 AM to arrive at sunrise. Bring snorkeling gear (or rent at the beach). The drive through the White Mountains is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort — enjoy the private beach, infinity pool, and world-class spa facilities. Optional: sunrise yoga session on the clifftop terrace (arrange with the resort).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private boat charter from Elounda to the mysterious island of Spinalonga — the last active leper colony in Europe, now a haunting and fascinating UNESCO-listed historical site. Explore with a private guide, then cruise the surrounding turquoise waters and swim in secluded coves.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Crete at a top restaurant in Agios Nikolaos, the chic lakeside town near Elounda.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the resort's terrace restaurant overlooking the bay
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the boat during the Spinalonga cruise — arrange a catered picnic with the charter company
meals.dinner: Dinner at Pelagos Restaurant in Agios Nikolaos — acclaimed seafood restaurant with exceptional fresh catch and Cretan wine list

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charter to Spinalonga can be arranged through the resort concierge. The island closes to visitors in the evening — plan the afternoon visit accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of the Crete resort. Transfer to Heraklion Airport for a short domestic flight to Santorini (Thira Airport). Upon arrival, transfer via private car or cable car to your luxury caldera-view hotel in Oia or Imerovigli (e.g., Canaves Oia Epitome, Grace Hotel Santorini, or Andronis Luxury Suites).
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into your clifftop suite with breathtaking caldera views. Explore the iconic blue-domed village of Oia on foot — browse art galleries, jewelry boutiques, and artisan shops along the narrow whitewashed lanes.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Oia's world-famous sunset from the castle ruins — arrive early to secure a prime spot. Afterward, enjoy a celebratory dinner at one of Santorini's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Crete resort before departure
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Oia upon arrival — try local tomato fritters (tomatokeftedes) and fava dip
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant at Andronis Luxury Suites — Michelin-recommended, dramatic caldera views, exceptional modern Greek cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Heraklion to Santorini flights are approximately 40 minutes. Alternatively, a high-speed ferry (2 hours) is a scenic option. Book Santorini accommodation well in advance — luxury caldera properties sell out months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Sunset Sailing and Swimming in the Caldera — join a private or small-group luxury catamaran cruise around Santorini's volcanic caldera. Stop at the iconic Red Beach (dramatic red volcanic cliffs), swim in the warm Aegean, and visit the hot springs near Nea Kameni volcanic island. Enjoy snorkeling in crystal-clear waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient site of Akrotiri — Santorini's remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age settlement, often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean.' Explore with a private guide. Afterward, visit the black-sand beach of Perissa or Perivolos for a relaxed swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for the legendary sunset, this time from a private terrace or rooftop bar. Enjoy a wine tasting of Santorini's unique Assyrtiko wines at a premium winery.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — enjoy on your private terrace with caldera views
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch served on the catamaran — fresh salads, grilled meats, local cheeses, and chilled Assyrtiko wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Selene Restaurant in Pyrgos — one of Santorini's most celebrated restaurants, showcasing the island's volcanic terroir through innovative Cycladic cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the private catamaran charter in advance — sunset cruises are extremely popular. The catamaran experience can be timed for either morning or afternoon depending on preference.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Santo Wines Winery for a private morning wine tasting — perched on the caldera rim with spectacular views, taste Santorini's distinctive volcanic wines including Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto dessert wine. Learn about the island's unique basket-trained vine cultivation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the medieval village of Pyrgos — Santorini's highest point, offering 360-degree island views. Visit the Byzantine castle ruins and charming artisan workshops. Alternatively, enjoy a private helicopter tour of the caldera and surrounding islands (arrange through the hotel concierge).
day_by_day.evening: Indulge in a couples' or solo spa treatment at your hotel's luxury spa — try a volcanic stone massage or a wine therapy treatment unique to Santorini. Enjoy a final caldera-view dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, local honey, Santorini cherry tomatoes, and eggs
meals.lunch: Lunch at Metaxy Mas in Exo Gonia — beloved local taverna serving exceptional traditional Santorinian dishes in a rustic setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Argo Restaurant in Fira — stunning caldera views, fresh seafood, and an extensive Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: Santo Wines morning tastings are quieter and more intimate than afternoon sessions. Book the helicopter tour at least 48 hours in advance through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning in Santorini — enjoy a slow breakfast on your private terrace, take a dip in your infinity pool, and soak in the caldera views. Optional: sunrise hike from Fira to Oia along the caldera rim trail (approximately 10 km, 3–4 hours) for extraordinary early morning views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a ferry or private speedboat transfer from Santorini to Zakynthos (via Athens or direct charter, approximately 3–4 hours total). Check in to your luxury villa or boutique hotel on Zakynthos (e.g., a private villa in the Vassilikos peninsula area).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the charming Zakynthos Town waterfront — stroll the Venetian-influenced harbor, visit the Byzantine Museum, and enjoy aperitifs at a waterfront café.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast in Santorini — enjoy every last caldera view moment
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Santorini port or on the ferry
meals.dinner: Welcome dinner in Zakynthos at Malanos Restaurant — a legendary local institution serving traditional Zakynthian cuisine with fresh seafood and local wines since 1949

day_by_day.notes: The Santorini–Zakynthos connection may require a connection through Athens or a private charter. Confirm routing and book well in advance. A private speedboat or seaplane charter is the most luxurious option.

day_by_day.morning: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Day Trip — take an early morning private boat excursion from Porto Vromi to the iconic Navagio Beach, one of Greece's most photographed locations. Arrive before the crowds to swim in the impossibly blue enclosed bay, explore the rusting shipwreck, and enjoy the towering white limestone cliffs in golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat excursion to the stunning Blue Caves on the northern tip of Zakynthos — snorkel in the electric-blue sea caves where sunlight refracts through the water creating an otherworldly glow. Return to the villa for a relaxed afternoon by the pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a clifftop viewpoint overlooking Navagio Beach (accessible by road from the top of the cliffs — a different and equally dramatic perspective). Enjoy a refined dinner at a top Zakynthos restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the villa or hotel before the boat departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on the private boat at Navagio Beach — fresh local produce, cheeses, charcuterie, and chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Nobelos Restaurant in Agios Nikolaos — elegant clifftop dining with panoramic Ionian Sea views and exceptional fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Porto Vromi by 7:00–7:30 AM to reach Navagio before the tour boats arrive. A private boat charter is strongly recommended for this experience. Bring sunscreen and water shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Zakynthos Marine Park and Laganas Bay — home to the endangered loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta). Join a responsible wildlife boat tour to observe turtles in their natural habitat. The warm June waters make this an ideal time for sightings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Venetian-influenced Zakynthos Town in depth — visit the Church of Saint Dionysios (patron saint of the island), the Solomos Museum, and the elegant Plateia Solomou square. Browse local shops for Zakynthian specialties including mandolato nougat and local olive oil.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner on Zakynthos — enjoy a long, leisurely meal celebrating the penultimate night of the trip with the finest local cuisine and wine.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the villa — fresh local produce, Zakynthian honey, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional taverna in Keri village — try local specialties including bourdeto (spicy fish stew) and sofrito
meals.dinner: Dinner at Prosilio Restaurant in Zakynthos Town — sophisticated modern Greek cuisine in an elegant setting with an outstanding Greek wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: The marine park turtle tours are strictly regulated — choose only certified eco-friendly operators. June is peak nesting season, making sightings highly likely.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning leisure — enjoy a slow breakfast at the villa, take a last swim in the Ionian Sea, and pack at a relaxed pace. Optional: visit the picturesque village of Keri and its lighthouse for sweeping views of the southern coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Zakynthos Airport (Dionysios Solomos Airport) for your departure flight back to Athens or directly to Belgrade. If time permits before the flight, enjoy a final coffee and pastry at a waterfront café in Zakynthos Town.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Zakynthos, carrying memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring Greece's finest beaches, flavors, and ancient wonders.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final breakfast at the villa — a full spread of Greek favorites: yogurt with honey, fresh fruit, pastries, eggs, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at a harbor café in Zakynthos Town — fresh salad, grilled fish, and a glass of local white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Athens airport lounge or on the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and arrange private transfer to Zakynthos Airport. Allow at least 2 hours before departure. Consider purchasing local specialties as gifts: Zakynthian olive oil, mandolato, Santorini Assyrtiko wine, and Cretan thyme honey.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
